# Plan: Hardcore Mode (permadeath, spectate-the-dead-world)

## Context

The difficulty axis just merged (PR #33, save v9). The one axis still flagged as deferred in
`lib/game/gameModes.ts` is the **Hardcore flag**. This adds it — a per-world, **immutable** boolean,
chosen at world creation, that makes a run high-stakes:

- **Locks Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces game mode = Survival and difficulty = Hard, and
  **disables both pause-menu switchers** (otherwise flipping to Creative/invulnerable or lowering
  difficulty would make permadeath meaningless).
- **Permadeath → spectate the dead world.** On death the run is permanently over: the player flips to a
  **spectator** free camera to roam their dead world, a persisted **`gameOver`** flag is set, and a
  **Game Over** screen offers *Spectate* / *Back to Worlds* / *Delete World*. Re-entering a dead world
  resumes the game-over+spectator state, never a fresh playable world.
- **Withered hearts.** A darker "hardcore" heart palette (zero new assets) signals the mode.

Hardcore is a **boolean flag**, not an enum — so unlike difficulty it needs no `accessor` module; the
locking/permadeath logic lives in the engine, threaded through the same per-world plumbing as `difficulty`.

## Approach

### 1. Persistence (save v9 → v10, world meta)

- `lib/game/types.ts` — rename current `SaveData` body → `SaveDataV9`; new current `SaveData` at
  `version: 10` adds optional `hardcore?: boolean` + `gameOver?: boolean`.
- `lib/game/save.ts` — add `migrateSaveV9toV10` (pure bump); chain it in `readSave` + change the terminal
  guard to `!== 10`; add `restoreHardcore(save)` / `restoreGameOver(save)` (both `=== true`, default false).
- `lib/game/worlds.ts` — add `hardcore: boolean` to `WorldMeta` (immutable); coerce in `sanitizeWorld`
  (`typeof entry.hardcore === "boolean" ? … : false`); accept `deps.hardcore` in `createWorld`. **No
  worlds-manifest version bump** (additive, like `difficulty`).

### 2. Engine: forcing, locks, and the game-over transition

- `lib/game/engine/state.ts` — add `hardcore: boolean` + `gameOver: boolean` to `GameState` (both
  persisted) and to `GameSnapshot`; add `{ type: "gameOver" }` to the `GameEvent` union.
- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`:
  - `GameEngineOptions.hardcore?: boolean`.
  - **Constructor precedence** — resolve hardcore/gameOver first, then let them override mode/difficulty:
    ```
    const hardcore = save ? restoreHardcore(save) : (options.hardcore ?? false);
    const gameOver = save ? restoreGameOver(save) : false;
    const difficulty = hardcore ? "hard" : (save ? restoreDifficulty(save) : (options.difficulty ?? "normal"));
    const gameMode = gameOver ? "spectator" : hardcore ? "survival" : (save ? restoreGameMode(save) : (options.gameMode ?? "survival"));
    ```
    `isFlying: gameMode === "spectator"` already yields a flying camera for a restored game-over. The
    constructor + step() auto-unstuck checks already gate on `!isNoclip(gameMode)`, so a restored dead
    world (spectator) is never teleported out of terrain — no change needed there.
  - **Death branch** — the only two lethal paths are the `applyDamage` and `applyEnvironmentalDamage`
    arrow methods (poison/starvation-floored use `applyNonLethalDamage`, never lethal). In each, when
    `died && state.hardcore`, call `this.triggerGameOver()` and `return` (skipping the normal
    `{type:"died"}` path). All sources (fall/void/mob/arrow/explosion/water/lava/drown/starvation-on-Hard)
    funnel through these two.
  - New **`triggerGameOver()`**: set `gameOver = true`; set `gameMode = "spectator"` **directly** (not via
    the locked `switchGameMode`); `isFlying = true`; `isDead = false` + `respawnTimer = 0` (so the respawn
    DeathScreen never shows); `hearts = 0`; `clearEffects` + `resetMining`; close panels + `paused = false`;
    `emit({ type: "gameOver" })`.
  - **Locks** — guard the top of `switchGameMode` and `switchDifficulty` with `if (state.hardcore) return;`
    so the `setGameMode`/`setDifficulty` commands no-op. The engine's own death→spectator bypasses this
    (sets `state.gameMode` inline). Difficulty stays `"hard"` for the world's life.
  - **`pause` guard** — extend the existing `victory` early-return to `victory || gameOver` so the pause
    menu can't open while spectating a dead world (the Game Over screen owns navigation).
  - **`serialize()`** — `version: 10`, add `hardcore: state.hardcore`, `gameOver: state.gameOver`.
  - `tickRespawnTimer` needs **no** hardcore guard (it early-returns on `!isDead`, always false post-game-over).

### 3. UI: creation toggle, locked switchers, Game Over screen, shell delete

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx` — add a **Hardcore toggle** (single `world-type-option`-style
  button, `aria-pressed`). When on, force + lock the Game Mode (Survival) and Difficulty (Hard) grids
  (render them disabled with the forced value) and submit `gameMode: "survival"`, `difficulty: "hard"`,
  `hardcore`. Extend `onCreate` signature with a trailing `hardcore`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx` — thread `hardcore` into `createWorld({ …, hardcore })`; show a
  `Hardcore · ` label on the world card (mirror the gameMode/difficulty labels).
- `components/game/PauseMenu.tsx` — add a `hardcore` prop; when true, render the Game Mode + Difficulty
  grids **disabled** with a "Locked (Hardcore)" note.
- `components/game/GameOverScreen.tsx` (NEW) — mirror `VictoryScreen.tsx`. Shown when `snapshot.gameOver`.
  Buttons: **Spectate World** (local `minimized` state → collapses to a small corner "☠ Game Over · Menu"
  re-open affordance so the player can fly the dead world while keeping Delete/Quit one click away),
  **Back to Worlds** (`onQuitToWorlds`), **Delete World** (confirm → `onDeleteWorld`).
- `components/GameShell.tsx` — add an `onDeleteWorld` callback to the play screen (mirror `onQuitToWorlds`):
  `deleteWorld(world.id)` + clear the session pointer + go to `world-select`. Thread it through
  `MinecraftGame` to `GameOverScreen`.
- `components/MinecraftGame.tsx` — destructure `hardcore`/`gameOver` from the hook; render
  `<GameOverScreen>`; pass `hardcore` to `PauseMenu` and `onDeleteWorld` through.
- `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` — `PRE_MOUNT_SNAPSHOT` gets `hardcore:false, gameOver:false`; add a
  `worldHardcoreRef` and pass `hardcore` into `new GameEngine({…})`; expose `hardcore`/`gameOver` from the
  snapshot. In the event loop, on **`gameOver`**: exit pointer lock + `clearKeys` (mirror `died`) **and
  force a synchronous save** (the engine has no storage handle), so closing the tab right after death still
  resumes the dead world.

### 4. HUD: withered hardcore hearts

- `lib/ui/hudPixels.ts` — add `heart_hardcore_full` / `heart_hardcore_half` / `heart_hardcore_container`
  to `HudIconName` + the `renderHudIconPixels` switch, painting `HEART_GRID` with new darker
  `HARDCORE_HEART_PALETTE` / `…_CONTAINER_PALETTE` (withered reds). `hudIconUrl` already keys by name.
- `components/game/StatusBars.tsx` — add a `hardcore` prop; the heart `IconRow` uses the `heart_hardcore`
  variant when true. Thread `hardcore` from snapshot → `MinecraftGame` → `StatusBars`.

# Plan: Hardcore Mode (permadeath, spectate-the-dead-world)

## Context

chosen at world creation, that makes a run high-stakes:

- **Locks Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces game mode = Survival and difficulty = Hard, and
  **disables both pause-menu switchers** (otherwise flipping to Creative/invulnerable or lowering
  difficulty would make permadeath meaningless).
- **Permadeath → spectate the dead world.** On death the run is permanently over: the player flips to a
  **spectator** free camera to roam their dead world, a persisted **`gameOver`** flag is set, and a
  **Game Over** screen offers *Spectate* / *Back to Worlds* / *Delete World*. Re-entering a dead world
  resumes the game-over+spectator state, never a fresh playable world.
- **Withered hearts.** A darker "hardcore" heart palette (zero new assets) signals the mode.

Hardcore is a **boolean flag**, not an enum — so unlike difficulty it needs no `accessor` module; the
locking/permadeath logic lives in the engine, threaded through the same per-world plumbing as `difficulty`.

### 1. Persistence (save v9 → v10, world meta)

  `version: 10` adds optional `hardcore?: boolean` + `gameOver?: boolean`.

  guard to `!== 10`; add `restoreHardcore(save)` / `restoreGameOver(save)` (both `=== true`, default false).
- `lib/game/worlds.ts` — add `hardcore: boolean` to `WorldMeta` (immutable); coerce in `sanitizeWorld`
  (`typeof entry.hardcore === "boolean" ? … : false`); accept `deps.hardcore` in `createWorld`. **No
  worlds-manifest version bump** (additive, like `difficulty`).

### 2. Engine: forcing, locks, and the game-over transition

- `lib/game/engine/state.ts` — add `hardcore: boolean` + `gameOver: boolean` to `GameState` (both
  persisted) and to `GameSnapshot`; add `{ type: "gameOver" }` to the `GameEvent` union.
- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`:
  - `GameEngineOptions.hardcore?: boolean`.

    ```

    const gameOver = save ? restoreGameOver(save) : false;
    const difficulty = hardcore ? "hard" : (save ? restoreDifficulty(save) : (options.difficulty ?? "normal"));

    funnel through these two.

    DeathScreen never shows); `hearts = 0`; `clearEffects` + `resetMining`; close panels + `paused = false`;

    (sets `state.gameMode` inline). Difficulty stays `"hard"` for the world's life.

    menu can't open while spectating a dead world (the Game Over screen owns navigation).

  grids **disabled** with a "Locked (Hardcore)" note.

  **Back to Worlds** (`onQuitToWorlds`), **Delete World** (confirm → `onDeleteWorld`).

  `deleteWorld(world.id)` + clear the session pointer + go to `world-select`. Thread it through
  `MinecraftGame` to `GameOverScreen`.

roamable dead world, not a playable one — which the existing noclip stuck-check

The two lethal seams (applyDamage, applyEnvironmentalDamage) divert to a new
triggerGameOver() when hardcore: it flips the player to a Spectator free-cam,
sets the persisted gameOver flag, and leaves isDead/respawnTimer cleared so the
respawn DeathScreen never shows (poison/starvation-floored can't kill, so they
need no branch). switchGameMode/switchDifficulty no-op under hardcore (the death
transition sets the mode directly, bypassing the lock), pause is blocked during
game-over, and serialize writes both flags.

  | "heart_half"

  | "hunger_full"

export function renderHudIconPixels(name: HudIconName): Uint8ClampedArray {
  switch (name) {

/** Left half of `full` over `container` — the classic half-heart/half-drumstick. */
function halfIcon(full: Uint8ClampedArray, container: Uint8ClampedArray): Uint8ClampedArray {
  const out = new Uint8ClampedArray(container);
  for (let y = 0; y < SPRITE_SIZE; y += 1) {
    for (let x = 0; x < SPRITE_SIZE / 2; x += 1) {
      const i = (y * SPRITE_SIZE + x) * 4;
      if (full[i + 3] === 0) continue;
      out[i] = full[i];
      out[i + 1] = full[i + 1];
      out[i + 2] = full[i + 2];
      out[i + 3] = full[i + 3];
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Game modes — the four Minecraft-style ways to play, a single per-player axis
 * the player picks at world creation and can switch in the pause menu:
 *
 * - **survival**  — the original game: gather, craft, fight, take damage.
 * - **creative**  — fly, build with unlimited blocks, invulnerable, instant break.
 * - **adventure** — survival, but terrain can't be broken or placed.
 * - **spectator** — fly through everything, unseen and unable to interact.
 *
 * Difficulty is a separate, orthogonal axis — it lives in lib/game/difficulties.ts
 * (Peaceful/Easy/Normal/Hard). The Hardcore flag remains deferred to a later change.
 *
 * Systems gate on the **predicates** below (intent: "can this mode edit
 * blocks?") rather than comparing the raw id, so a new mode only has to answer
 * the predicates and every call site keeps working.
 */

An axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, and likewise **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ difficulty. Restored by `restoreDifficulty` (`lib/game/save.ts`); the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts`, the starvation accumulator (`starvationTimer`) is session-only

Difficulty is an axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, switchable in-game, so the _current_ level is what's stored; the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` and the `starvationTimer` accumulator is session-only. No worldgen change — difficulty touches no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.

The constructor resolves it first so it overrides the other axes — forced to Survival + Hard — and `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` early-return under it (the player-facing switchers are disabled; the engine's own death transition sets the mode directly, bypassing the lock). ## Difficulty

A separate dial from the game mode, picked next to it at world creation and
switchable any time from the **pause menu** (`Esc` → Difficulty). It's saved with
the world and sets _how hard_ survival is — monster numbers, how hard they hit, and
whether an empty hunger bar can kill you.

- **Peaceful** — no monsters spawn (and switching to Peaceful clears any already
  around), health regenerates twice as fast, and an empty hunger bar never hurts
  you. Full survival — gather, build, mine — minus the danger.
- **Easy** — fewer monsters and they hit at half strength; starving stops at 5
  hearts.
- **Normal** — the balanced default; starving chips you down to half a heart but no
  further.
- **Hard** — monsters spawn thick and hit 1.5× as hard, and **starving can kill
  you**.

Flipping to Peaceful mid-fight is a safe panic button — every hostile (even the
boss) vanishes at once.

boss) vanishes at once.

## Hardcore

A toggle on the new-world form for players who want the ultimate stakes. A Hardcore
world is **locked to Survival + Hard** — you can't switch game mode or lower the
difficulty (the pause-menu switchers are greyed out), so there's no escape hatch.
Its hearts are drawn in a darker, withered red so you always know you're in it.

The defining rule: **death is permanent.** There's no respawn. When you die the run
is over — the world becomes a **dead world** you can only spectate: a free camera
that flies through everything while a **Game Over** screen offers to *Spectate*
(roam your dead world), go *Back to Worlds*, or *Delete World*. Reloading a dead
world drops you back into that same spectating state; it can never be played again.
Choose Hardcore knowing every fall, creeper, and empty hunger bar could be the last.

# Monecraft (Next.js + TypeScript + Three.js + Bun)

[![CI](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/hutusi/monecraft?label=release&sort=semver)](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/tags)

A playable, Minecraft-inspired voxel game that runs entirely in your browser. Explore procedural terrain across five biomes and dig into **dark caves** — lit only by the torches you craft and place, where lava pools and mobs lurk. Mine ores, raid **underground dungeons** for loot, build and farm, breed animals, craft through seven gear tiers up to a **bow** and throwable **spears**, and take on an **endgame boss** for a true win condition — all across a day-night cycle with hunger, drowning, and lava hazards.

The twist: **everything is procedural — zero binary assets.** Block textures and item sprites are painted from pixel code, all sound and music is synthesized at runtime, and lighting is computed per voxel. Single-player and client-only: keep **multiple worlds** under **multiple player profiles**, all saved to localStorage.

## Run

```bash
bun install
bun run dev
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000`.

The game opens to a menu: pick or create a **profile** (your name and look), then create or choose a **world** to play. New worlds let you pick a **type** — Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands — a **game mode**, a **difficulty** (Peaceful · Easy · Normal · Hard), and a seed. Each profile keeps its own list of worlds, so several players can share one browser. Inside the game, **Esc → Save & Quit to Worlds** returns to the world list.

## Controls

- `W A S D`: Move · `Space`: Jump · `C`: Crouch
- `W + CapsLock`: Sprint (drains hunger)
- Double-tap `Space`: Toggle flight in Creative (Spectator always flies); then `Space` / `C` to rise / descend
- `Mouse`: Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)
- `Left click` (hold): Break block / attack mobs
- `Right click` or `E`: Place/interact, or throw a selected spear
- `1..9`: Select hotbar slot
- `I`: Inventory & crafting · `F`: Eat food · `Shift+U`: Emergency unstuck
- `V`: Camera view (first-person → third-person rear → third-person front)
- `Esc`: Pause menu — three tabs: **Game** (save / load / reset, **Save & Quit to Worlds**, the **Game Mode** and **Difficulty** switchers), **Options** (sound/music volume, Appearance skins), and **Controls** · `F3`: Debug overlay

New here? The [player manual](docs/manual.md) walks through your first day, survival, crafting, farming, mobs, and more.

## Development

```bash
bun run lint        # ESLint
bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
bun test            # unit + integration + component tests
bun run build       # production build
bun run test:e2e    # Playwright browser smoke tests
bun run format      # Prettier
```

All of these are enforced by CI on every PR. The game simulation is a headless engine (no DOM), so gameplay logic is covered by real simulation tests, and a Playwright smoke suite exercises the browser layers — see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md).

## Docs

- [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md) — player guide: getting started, survival, crafting, mobs, farming
- [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md) — scannable tables: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item stats
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — engine/renderer/shell layering and invariants
- [docs/adding-content.md](docs/adding-content.md) — add a block, item, recipe, mob, or mechanic
- [docs/save-format.md](docs/save-format.md) — save schema and compatibility rules
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — workflow and verification baseline

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Hardcore mode**: a per-world **permadeath** toggle on the new-world form, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v9 → v10** (additive `hardcore` + `gameOver`), with **no worldgen change**
  - **Locked to Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces the game mode to Survival and the difficulty to Hard and **disables both pause-menu switchers** (immutable for the world's life), so there's no flipping to Creative or lowering the difficulty to cheat death. Its hearts render in a darker **withered** variant (a recolour of the procedural heart sprite)
  - **Death is permanent → spectate the dead world.** On death there is no respawn: the player flips to a **Spectator** free camera over their dead world (mobs keep roaming but can't touch them) and a **Game Over** screen offers _Spectate World_ (minimizes so you can fly around), _Back to Worlds_, or _Delete World_. The `gameOver` flag persists, so reloading a dead world resumes spectating — it can never be played again
  - **Architecture**: `hardcore` is a per-world boolean (`WorldMeta` + a v10 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV9toV10`), resolved first in the engine so it overrides mode/difficulty. The two lethal damage seams divert to a new `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()` (sets `gameOver`, switches to spectator, leaves `isDead` cleared so the respawn screen never shows); `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` no-op under hardcore (the death transition sets the mode directly); the shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event. New `GameOverScreen` component + a `GameShell` delete-world path
- **Difficulty**: the game gains Minecraft's difficulty axis

2	
3	Scannable tables for everything in the game: recipes, blocks, mobs, and item
4	stats. For how it all fits together, read the [player manual](manual.md).
5	
6	> **The code is the source of truth.** These tables are a convenience snapshot of
7	> `lib/game/recipes.ts`, `lib/game/items.ts`, `lib/world/blocks.ts`,
8	> `lib/game/mobs.ts`, and `lib/game/mobLoot.ts`. If a number here disagrees with
9	> the game, the code wins — and this page needs an update.
10	
11	## Game modes
12	
13	Chosen at world creation and switchable any time from the pause menu; saved with
14	the world and independent of the world type. Source: `lib/game/gameModes.ts` (the
15	`GameMode` union + predicates each system gates on).
16	
17	| Mode      | Damage / hunger | Break / place blocks   | Flight       | Interact (combat, doors, eat) | Mobs       | Inventory         |
18	| --------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
19	| Survival  | Yes             | Yes                    | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
20	| Creative  | No (invincible) | Instant, free (no use) | Yes          | Yes                           | Ignore you | All-items palette |
21	| Adventure | Yes             | **No**                 | No           | Yes                           | Hostile    | Normal            |
22	| Spectator | No (invincible) | No                     | Yes (noclip) | **No**                        | Ignore you | Hidden            |
23	
24	## Difficulty
25	
26	A separate axis from the game mode — also chosen at world creation, switchable from
27	the pause menu, and saved with the world. Sets how hard survival is. Source:
28	`lib/game/difficulties.ts` (the `Difficulty` union + accessors each system reads).
29	
30	| Level    | Hostiles spawn             | Mob damage | Spawn rate / cap  | Starvation            |
31	| -------- | -------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------- | --------------------- |
32	| Peaceful | No (and despawns existing) | —          | none / 0          | Never (regen ×2 fast) |
33	| Easy     | Yes                        | ×0.5       | slower / cap 8    | Stops at 5 hearts     |
34	| Normal   | Yes                        | ×1.0       | baseline / cap 16 | Stops at ½ heart      |
35	| Hard     | Yes                        | ×1.5       | faster / cap 24   | Kills you             |
36	
37	## Hardcore
38	
39	A per-world toggle (immutable, chosen at creation) for permadeath. Forces \*\*Survival
40	
41	- Hard\*\* and locks both switchers. On death the run ends: the world flips to a
42	  spectator "dead world" with a Game Over screen (Spectate / Back to Worlds / Delete
43	  World), and the dead state persists across reloads. Hearts render in a withered
44	  dark-red variant. Source: the `hardcore`/`gameOver` flags in `lib/game/types.ts` +
45	  `GameEngine.triggerGameOver`.
46	
47	## World types
48	
49	Chosen when you create a world (alongside the name and seed) and fixed for its
50	life. All four share the same five biomes — they reshape terrain, not the biome
51	mix. Source: `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` + `terrainConfigFor` in `lib/world/generation.ts`.
52	
53	| Type      | Terrain                                                                                     |
54	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
55	| Default   | Balanced terrain with every biome — the original generator                                  |
56	| Superflat | Level ground at a fixed height; a builder's canvas (caves and ores still generate below)    |
57	| Amplified | Exaggerated relief — towering peaks and deep valleys                                        |
58	| Islands   | A raised sea breaks the land into scattered, gently sloped islands with deep ocean channels |
59	
60	## Recipes
61	
62	**66 crafting recipes** (plus **10 villager trades**, listed under [Trading](#trading)).
63	All use the always-available crafting grid except the nine **furnace** smelting
64	recipes (need an open furnace) and the five **brewing** recipes (need an open
65	[brewing stand](#brewing--potions)).

1	# Player Manual
2	
3	A complete guide to playing Monecraft — a single-player, browser-based voxel
4	sandbox. Mine, build, craft, farm, fight off the night, and survive.
5	
6	This page is the prose guide; for the exact numbers (every recipe, block, mob, and
7	item stat) see the [reference tables](reference.md). Just want the keys? They're in
8	the [README](../README.md#controls).
9	
10	> Everything you see and hear is generated from code at runtime — there are no
11	> image or audio files anywhere in the game.
12	
13	## Worlds & profiles
14	
15	The game opens to a menu rather than dropping you straight into a world:
16	
17	1. **Pick a profile.** A profile is a player — a name and an appearance (skin). On a
18	   shared browser everyone can have their own. Create one with **New Profile**, choose
19	   a skin, and you're in; rename or delete profiles from the same screen.
20	2. **Pick a world.** Each profile keeps its **own** list of worlds. **New World** lets
21	   you name it, choose a **world type** (Default, Superflat, Amplified, or Islands —
22	   see [the reference](reference.md#world-types)), and optionally enter a **seed** —
23	   type a number or a word to get the same world every time, or leave it blank for a
24	   random one. Worlds you've played show most-recent first; rename or delete them here too.
25	3. **Play.** Choosing a world drops you in. From the pause menu (**Esc**), **Save &
26	   Quit to Worlds** takes you back to the list, and reloading the page resumes the
27	   world you were in.
28	
29	Everything is saved in your browser (localStorage). Deleting a world removes its save;
30	deleting a profile removes all of its worlds.
31	
32	## Getting started: your first day
33	
34	You spawn at dawn on solid ground with a small starter kit: stacks of grass, dirt,
35	stone, wood, planks, cobble, and sand, plus a **wood pickaxe** and a **knife**.
36	
37	The day-night cycle is short — **four minutes per full day** — so the first night
38	comes fast. A good opening:
39	
40	1. **Look around.** Double-click the game to lock the mouse (the starting gesture
41	   doesn't mine). Move with `W A S D`, look with the mouse.
42	2. **Gear up from your kit.** Open the inventory with **`I`**. You already have
43	   cobble and wood, so craft a **stone pickaxe** (2 cobble + 1 wood) and a **stone
44	   sword** (2 cobble + 1 wood) — both upgrades over your starting wood pickaxe and
45	   knife.
46	3. **Mine and gather.** Hold **left-click** to break trees, stone, and dirt for
47	   more materials; craft **2 wood → 4 planks** whenever you need them.
48	4. **Shelter before dark.** Wall yourself in with blocks (**right-click** or `E`
49	   to place the selected hotbar item), or craft a **bed** and skip the night
50	   entirely. Hostile mobs spawn once it gets dark, so don't be caught in the open.
51	
52	From there it's a sandbox: dig for ores, build, farm, breed animals, and gear up.
53	
54	## Controls
55	
56	| Key / input        | Action                                                                                                        |
57	| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
58	| `W` `A` `S` `D`    | Move (walk / strafe)                                                                                          |
59	| `Space`            | Jump                                                                                                          |
60	| `C`                | Crouch (slower, careful movement)                                                                             |
61	| `W` + `CapsLock`   | Sprint — faster, but drains hunger                                                                            |
62	| Double-tap `Space` | Toggle flight in Creative (Spectator always flies); `Space` / `C` rise/descend while flying                   |
63	| Mouse              | Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)                                                 |
64	| Left-click (hold)  | Break the targeted block / attack a mob                                                                       |
65	| Right-click or `E` | Place/interact, or throw a selected spear                                                                     |
66	| `1`–`9`            | Select a hotbar slot                                                                                          |
67	| `I`                | Open / close inventory & crafting                                                                             |
68	| `F`                | Eat the selected food, or drink a selected potion                                                             |
69	| `V`                | Cycle camera: first-person → third-person rear → third-person front                                           |

## What it does

- **Locked to Survival + Hard.** A hardcore world forces game mode = Survival and difficulty = Hard and **disables both pause-menu switchers** — no flipping to Creative (invulnerable) or lowering difficulty to dodge death. Hearts render in a darker **withered** variant (a recolour of the procedural heart sprite).

The `gameOver` flag persists, so reloading a dead world resumes spectating — it can never be played again.

## How it's built

`hardcore` is a per-world boolean (`WorldMeta` + a v10 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV9toV10`), resolved **first** in the `GameEngine` constructor so it overrides mode/difficulty. ## PR #34 — `feat: hardcore mode (permadeath)`
https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/pull/34

This closes out the **last axis `gameModes.ts` had deferred** (game modes → difficulty → hardcore).

### What shipped (your chosen spec)
- **Spectate-the-dead-world permadeath** — on death the player flips to a Spectator free-cam over their dead world; a Game Over screen offers Spectate / Back to Worlds / Delete World; the `gameOver` flag persists so reloading resumes spectating, never playable again.
- **Locks Survival + Hard** — both pause-menu switchers disabled; the engine forces and guards them.
- **Withered hearts** — a darker procedural heart palette on hardcore worlds.

### 6 focused commits
save v10 persistence → engine forcing/locks/`triggerGameOver` → UI (toggle + locked switchers + GameOverScreen + GameShell delete) → withered hearts → docs → e2e.

### A few design calls worth your eye in review
- **`triggerGameOver` branches at the two lethal seams only** (the Plan agent confirmed poison/starvation-floored can't kill) and leaves `isDead` cleared, so the respawn screen never flashes.
- **Game-over persists, but `isDead`/`respawnTimer` stay session-only** — the dead state is captured by the new `gameOver` flag instead, and a restored spectator is left un-teleported by the existing `!isNoclip` stuck-check.
- **Shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event** so closing the tab right after death still resumes the dead world.

### Verify gate — all green
lint, typecheck, format, **771 unit**, build, **17 e2e** (incl. a new hardcore-creation check).

CI will re-run on the branch. As with the difficulty PR, I'll wait for any CodeRabbit review — say the word if you'd like me to check it once it lands. One thing I flagged in the PR body: the **death→spectator visuals aren't headless-verifiable**, so a manual gameplay pass is worth doing before you eventually cut a release.
